results.answer: Corporate governance refers to the system of rules, practices, and processes by which a company is directed and controlled, involving the balancing of interests among shareholders, senior management, customers, suppliers, financiers, the government, and the community.
contexts:
What is Corporate Governance?
Corporate governance refers to the system of rules, practices, and processes by which a company is
directed and controlled. It essentially involves balancing the interests of a company's many stakeholders,
such as shareholders, senior management executives, customers, suppliers, financiers, the government,
and the community.
Good corporate governance is fundamental to the long-term success and sustainability of any
organization. It provides the framework for attaining a company's objectives and encompasses practically
every sphere of management, from action plans and internal controls to performance measurement and
corporate disclosure.

Shareholder Rights
Protecting and facilitating the exercise of shareholder rights is a cornerstone of good corporate
governance. Shareholders are the owners of the company and must be provided with adequate
mechanisms to exercise their rights effectively.

Board of Directors
The board of directors is the highest governing authority within the management structure at any
publicly-traded company. It is elected by the shareholders to represent their interests and oversee the
management of the organization.
Board Composition
A well-structured board should consist of a majority of independent directors. The recommended board
size is between seven and fifteen members depending on the size and complexity of the organization. The
board must include at minimum three independent non-executive directors.

What is Corporate Governance?
Corporate governance refers to the system of rules, practices, and processes by which a company is
directed and controlled. It essentially involves balancing the interests of a company's many stakeholders,
such as shareholders, senior management executives, customers, suppliers, financiers, the government,
and the community.
Good corporate governance is fundamental to the long-term success and sustainability of any
organization. It provides the framework for attaining a company's objectives and encompasses practically
every sphere of management, from action plans and internal controls to performance measurement and
corporate disclosure.
Accountability Transparency Fairness

Transparency and Disclosure
The corporate governance framework must ensure that timely and accurate disclosure is made on all
material matters regarding the corporation, including its financial situation, performance, ownership, and
governance structure.

Audit and Risk Committee
The Audit and Risk Committee is a sub-committee of the board of directors. Its primary purpose is to assist
the board in fulfilling its oversight responsibilities for the financial reporting process, the audit process, the
company's system of internal controls, and compliance with laws and regulations.
Committee Composition Requirements
The Audit and Risk Committee must consist of a minimum of three members, all of whom must be
independent non-executive directors. At least one member must have relevant financial expertise, defined
as experience in finance, accounting, or related financial management. The committee chair must not be
the same person as the board chair.
Key Functions
Financial Reporting Internal Audit External Audit

governance. At least fifty percent of board members must be independent directors when the positions of
Chair and CEO are held by the same person.
